Definition: to emaciate, i.e. make (become) thin (literally or figuratively)
BiblicalUsage: Razah is to make thin, to emaciate. Isaiah says, 'And in that day it shall come to pass, that the glory of Jacob shall be made thin, and the fatness of his flesh shall wax lean'; and Zephaniah says the LORD 'will famish all the gods of the earth.'
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the thinning is judgment's shape: Jacob's glory made thin, and the gods of the earth famished — God makes lean what men made fat.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
